messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx error rate in eu-west-1 for /v1/generate (p95 latency up). Aggregated error rate 12% over last 2m. Paging: #oncall

alex.sre: getting the page. looking at the dashboards now. can someone confirm if this is regional only or per-AZ?

maya.netops: tracing the network overlays — I see packet loss spikes in eu-west-1a -> transit gateway around 03:12 UTC. route flaps + BGP withdraws logged.

jamie-prod: customer reports coming in: 3 customers hit increased latency, one 429 spike. listing accounts with errors: acct-231, acct-782.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/region-failover (link).

alex.sre: quick mitigation idea — shift weighted routing away from eu-west-1 to eu-west-2 temporarily, then drain instances in affected AZ. can we change Route53 health check policy?

maya.netops: i can adjust route weights but healthchecks are stuck failing due to DNS UDP fragments getting dropped in eu-west-1a. if we just change weights to 0 for eu-west-1 it will immediately send traffic to eu-west-2/gh.

lily-platform: note: we have sticky session behavior for embeddings sessions, need to ensure stateful endpoints are handled by fallback policy. might need cache key flush.

diego-oncall: i'm taking oncall. starting traffic-shift plan. tagging @jamie-prod for customer comms.

jamie-prod: preparing status message. ETA 10m for preliminary mitigation.

alex.sre: commands I'll run (rolling):
```bash
# set route53 weights to move traffic off eu-west-1
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes": [{"Action": "UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet": {"Name": "api.redwood.example","Type": "A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1","Weight":0}}]}'
```

maya.netops: after weight change, watch for unhealthy hosts in eu-west-2 getting overloaded. we should cap concurrency on eu-west-2 before shifting more than 60%.

alex.sre: starting weight change now (going to 30% -> 60% -> 0 in steps).

incident-bot: [ACTION] Route53 change submitted (change-id C123456).

jamie-prod: Status update to customers: "We're investigating degraded API performance affecting EU region. We're shifting traffic to healthy regions to mitigate. No data loss suspected. We'll update in 15 minutes." :loudspeaker:

lily-platform: i'm enabling per-model fallback to the smaller quantized variant in eu-west-2 to reduce CPU/GPU load during the shift:
```json
{"model":"rwd-xl-q4","fallback":"rwd-xl-q8","policy":"prefer-local-then-fallback"}
```

maya.netops: weight change to 60% applied. current global distribution: eu-west-1: 40% -> 20% -> now 15% (progressive), eu-west-2: +. Observing 20% increase in connection churn to eu-west-2 but healthy.

alex.sre: trimming load on problematic AZ by draining instances in eu-west-1a:
```bash
rcli drain-instances --region eu-west-1 --az eu-west-1a --tag affected=true
```

maya.netops: FYI: BGP control plane flaps continue intermittently. after we drain, we should remove eu-west-1a from LB target groups until stability.

diego-oncall: draining eu-west-1a now. starting with non-critical pools. I'll pause if error rates spike.

incident-bot: [NOTIFICATION] Handoff: diego-oncall is now primary responder for INC-2026-0421 (picked up at 1728004500).

jamie-prod: customers updated: added note about potential brief increases in latency during failover.

alex.sre: after 10m of progressive shifting, eu-west-1 overall 5xx down to 1.9%. eu-west-2 p95 latency up 30ms but within SLO.

lily-platform: I see cache key invalidations in progress, some sessions will reconnect but requests should succeed against eu-west-2.

maya.netops: new problem: Route53 health checks for eu-west-1 are flapping between healthy/unhealthy due to intermittent DNS TTL propagation issues; some clients still resolving to eu-west-1 IPs for TTL duration. TTL is 30s but we see stale resolutions for ~90s in some carriers.

alex.sre: can we add a policy to return 302 redirect to eu-west-2 for known HTTP callers? risky for streaming endpoints. prefer keeping routing-layer change.

diego-oncall: starting edge-level denylist for problematic carriers that continue to land in eu-west-1. doing blocklist for ASNs that show the stale cache.

jamie-prod: customer impact: 7 enterprise customers saw degraded experience during the window, one (acct-231) reported errors affecting billing APIs. ops is preparing a timeline for postmortem + customer RCA.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] Automated rollback guard: if eu-west-2 CPU > 85% for 3m, we will pause further weight increases.

alex.sre: monitoring shows eu-west-2 CPU peaked at 78% during biggest step, good margin. proceeding to set eu-west-1 weight to 0 now.

maya.netops: applied weight=0 for eu-west-1. global traffic stabilized to eu-west-2 and us-east variants. DNS propagation still trailing for some clients but impact minimal now.

diego-oncall: eu-west-1a removed from target groups. I'll keep it out until BGP stability confirmed. leaving maintenance marker on hosts.

jamie-prod: public status updated: "Mitigation complete: traffic shifted to healthy regions and affected AZ drained. We continue to monitor and will publish a postmortem." :white_check_mark:

lily-platform: follow-ups: add runbook step to TTL-toughness note, add automated edge-redirect for non-streaming endpoints during regional failover, and add better pre-shift capacity gating.

alex.sre: agree. also need improvement on cross-region cache warmup so eu-west-2 isn't cold on first heavy shift. creating ticket.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 acknowledged as mitigated at 1728004921. Postmortem assigned to alex.sre, maya.netops.

diego-oncall: handing back to oncall rotation, leaving detailed notes in incident doc. good job team. :clap:
